newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar still weak but holds above lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar still weak but holds above lows.

text.p: White sugar futures retained their earlier weakness in solid Wednesday trading but still managed to bounce back from the lows.
Some interest was noted in nearby August/October, which traded between $3.50 and $4.00. Volume was boosted by trade crosses after earlier commission house activity.
August, not front month after the May expiry on Tuesday, slumped to an intraday low of $306.70 but then managed to claw back some lost ground as New York fought its way higher.
"August has been offered down quite heavily on the back of the large deliveries that took place in London," said one trader.
London's May futures contract saw a hefty physical delivery of nearly 90,000 tonnes of sugar from British, Dutch, German and Spanish ports. The two receivers were Prudential Bache and Sucre Export.
At 1520 GMT May was down 20 cents at $308.40 and August down $1.10 at $303.60. Volume was 1,603 lots.
Little interest was seen in arbitrage activity against New York although some sellers were waiting in the wings to cap any gains.
"There are a few sellers around scale-up but no more than that," the trader said.
The Paris market saw more subdued activity with just 203 lots traded.
August was 50 cents lower at $307.80 and October 90 cents lower at $303.50.
